Adjusted read using SLOOS:
- Policy tone: still moderately hawkish on its face (“ongoing increases,” continued QT, higher administered rates), signaling tighter financial conditions.
- SLOOS cross-check: banks tightened lending standards for C&I and CRE; loan demand weakened across nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily; and banks cited decreased financing needs for plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, and accounts receivable. Foreign banks also reported weaker C&I demand. This indicates a meaningful credit tightening via the bank channel.
- Implication: the SLOOS suggests de facto additional restraint beyond the policy rate, aligning with the Committee’s emphasis on cumulative tightening and lags, and tempering the hawkishness implied by “ongoing increases.” Net tone is slightly negative, but more balanced than a rate/QT-only read.
